one_month_reasoning: Q4 FY26 results came out 2026-09-30, so the next Jabil earnings (Q1 FY27) are expected mid/late December, outside the window. The stock fell 10% on results day ($318.84 to $286.86) and then recovered to $304.41 within two days. That is a mixed post-event signal: a beat-and-raise (FY27 core EPS $17.55 vs ~$16.92 consensus) combined with a 'sell the news' reaction, light gross margins and a back-end-loaded margin ramp. In-window catalysts are sector-level: AI-hardware sentiment (the July-August AI selloff, the Celestica equity raise), hyperscaler Q3 earnings in late October with capex commentary, and macro prints. Hyperscaler capex guides could move the stock either way, so I see no clear directional edge. I used a near-symmetric lognormal centered at ~$305 with monthly sigma ~13% (47%/3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (FY28E core EPS $20.50 x 16x = $328) and FCF yield (FY28E adj. FCF $1.8B at a 5.5% yield over ~101M shares = $324), each weighted 50%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 (NTM as of Oct-2027) core EPS ~$20.50 x 16x forward multiple

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 guide $17.55 grown ~17%: low-teens revenue growth (networking growing 45-50% offset by declining Connected Living, which is down 15%), plus margin expansion from the back-end-loaded capacity ramp, plus ~3% annual share shrink from ~$1B/yr buybacks. Hyperscaler capex forecasts of ~$1-1.3T in 2027 support continued demand.

Flex traded at ~18.2x and JBL at ~19x NTM in mid-2026 (Nasdaq/Zacks). JBL trades at ~17.2x now. I applied a ~1x discount for AI-hardware sentiment (sector selloff, Celestica equity raise) and recession risk priced into 2027, which leaves it well below Celestica's ~30x.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 adj. FCF ~$1.8B / 5.5% target yield = $32.7B equity; ~101M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 $1.6B grown ~12%, below EPS growth because capex runs at 1.5-2% of revenue and inventory sits at 64 days vs the 55-60 target.
The current price implies ~5.0% on FY27 FCF ($1.6B / $31.9B market cap). I used a slightly higher yield to reflect cyclical AI-capex risk and net debt of ~$2.3B.
106.0M diluted in Q4 FY26 (104.8M outstanding), less ~3-4% from buybacks at the FY26 pace of ~$1.06B.

bear.story: AI capex digestion or a 2027 recession (Kalshi prices ~41%): networking and cloud orders slow, the 4M sq ft capacity ramp runs underutilized, FY28 EPS stalls near $17, and the multiple compresses to ~12x as the AI-hardware trade unwinds further.

base.story: Jabil delivers roughly the FY27 guide ($44.5B revenue, $17.55 EPS, 6.1% margin), the street models FY28 EPS ~$20.5, and the stock holds a 16x multiple, a modest discount to EMS peers given AI-cycle skepticism.

bull.story: Hyperscaler capex heads to $1.3T in 2027 per Nvidia/S&P, the capacity ramp reaches high utilization, margins exit FY27 above 6.5%, FY28 EPS reaches ~$22, and the multiple re-rates toward 20x as AI-hardware sentiment recovers. The stock retests the $429 high.

thesis_break_reason: Around $215 (~13x FY27 guided EPS, below the March-2026 trough area) the market would be pricing a cut to the FY27 guide or a hyperscaler order pause rather than multiple noise. That would most likely mean the AI-infrastructure demand or the capacity ramp economics broke.

reasoning: Basic facts: FY26 revenue was $36.0B and core EPS $13.09. The FY27 guide is $44.5B revenue, $17.55 core EPS (+34%), ~$1.6B adjusted FCF and a 6.1% core margin. Net debt is ~$2.3B and diluted shares are ~106M. The stock trades at ~17.3x FY27 guidance after falling 29% from the June high of $428.93. That decline came during a sector-wide AI-hardware selloff: forum and newsletter chatter cited Burry's shorts, China's Kimi 3 model, a hedge-fund blowup and Celestica's $3B equity raise. On 9/30 the stock fell 10% despite the beat. The StreetSignal Substack attributed this to the FY27 raise being smaller than the Q4 beat alone, light gross margins and a back-end-loaded ramp. The transcript adds that networking is growing 45-50%, Connected Living is down 15%, and inventory sits at 64 days. Alt/industry signals are supportive on demand: Moody's, S&P and Nvidia's CFO see hyperscaler capex at ~$1-1.3T in 2027, and the Rowan County, NC AI rack plant (1,181 jobs) starts hiring in 2026. On the macro side, Kalshi prices a 2027 recession at ~41% ($544K volume, per aggregator reports, early Oct 2026). Fair value comes out around $325 (16x FY28E EPS of $20.5; 5.5% FCF yield). That is ~7% above spot, so I put the median slightly above $304. Using the stock's 47% realized vol as a guide, I modeled the distribution as an 85/15 mixture of lognormals: main sigma 0.38 centered at $322, plus a bear tail centered at $215 with sigma 0.40. The scenarios bracket it: bear $200 (25%), base $330 (50%), bull $440 (25%). Limits: X/Twitter content was not reachable via search, the Twelve Data analyst-target endpoint required a higher plan, and I could not fetch a prediction-market page with the exact 2027 recession price, so that figure comes from aggregator snippets.
